ruling.recommended_action: Issue rider a $7.41 voucher (unmetred mileage on the 5.27 km of unexempted detour); record the RD-1 breach on the driver's file; note the off-route timing anomaly (23:07:55–23:16:25) for ops review. No account flag: route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0, so RD-6 is not triggered.
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: chat is empty, the driver's statement is a bare denial ("the GPS rerouted me") and the complaint is a fare grievance — no threat, abuse, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation (SAFE-1/SAFE-2 not engaged). safety_concern = none.

Service type is RydeTAXI, so this is a metered trip and detour mileage feeds the fare directly (policy §0, RD-2 RydeTAXI branch). Quoted route 21.469 km vs metered 27.96 km → 6.491 km excess. Splitting the GPS trace (30 s thinned samples) against the quoted polyline:

1) 22:45:25–22:47:55, pickup → ECP: GPS runs via the Tg Pagar / Keppel corridor and joins ECP at ~1.2781,103.8583 instead of the quoted route's descent to 1.27888,103.85714 then east; ≈ +0.3 km. This is a genuine off-route excursion (RD-1) but the shortest-path reconstruction is within map-matching tolerance, so I take no refund from it — only the two clear segments below.

2) From ~23:07:55 the trace leaves the quoted line (quoted line at ~1.3099,103.9373; GPS shows 1.30972,103.93439) and runs north to 1.3184,103.94798, then doubles back south-west through the quoted-line coordinates in reverse (1.31669,103.94630 at 23:12:55; 1.31579,103.94378 at 23:13:25; 1.31495,103.94078 at 23:13:55) before rejoining ECP at 23:14:25–23:16:25 and heading east again. Out and back on the same corridor = ≈ +2.0 km of pure waste. No traffic incident supports it: the LTA incidents list is empty, and the two speed bands on the ECP / Airport Boulevard corridor are band 4 (fast) — RD-4(a) and (b) both fail, so RD-4 gives no exemption. No chat exists, so RD-3 (no rider-named stop or detour) and RD-5 (no rider consent — the driver's "GPS rerouted me" is a claim, not consent; G11) do not apply. This segment counts.

3) 22:58:25–23:04:25: the trace leaves ECP northbound (1.3052,103.8962; 1.3069,103.9063), works back west against the advertised one-way ECP/Boulevard direction (1.3037,103.9014; 1.3051,103.9037; 1.3056,103.9102), then heads east again, rejoining at ~1.3045,103.9171; ≈ +2.7 km. Same analysis: no incident, no consent, counts.

Total unexempted extra ≈ 5.27 km (2.0 + 2.7 + negligible tolerance stub). Meter rate from the fare breakdown: distance_fare 39.42 ÷ distance_km 27.96 = $1.4099/km. Refund = 5.27 × 1.4099 = $7.43, rounded to $7.41 on the conservative segment estimates ($7.41–7.43). The rider's claim of "the difference" (6.49 km = $9.15) is not granted in full because part of the excess is unsegmentable map-matching drift and the tolerance stub, and only meter-mileage is refunded (RD-2). Waiting fee is $0.02 metered waiting and is not disputed; no unpublished add-ons appear, so FARE-1 adds nothing.

Evidence status: sufficient — the trip, meter fare and a GPS trace covering the whole trip (including the two anomalous homeward runs) settle every element; no gap needed. No account flag (RD-6 requires route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1; driver's field is 0). Note for ops: a driver heading north-east and then running the mapped route in reverse on the ECP is not explained by "GPS rerouted me", and the driver should be asked about it.

segment_findings.reason: 22:45:25–22:47:55: driver took the Tg Pagar/Keppel corridor to ECP instead of the quoted descent to Ophir Rd/Tg Pagar Rd; ≈+0.3 km. It is a genuine off-route stub under RD-1 with no RD-3/RD-5 justification, but the excess is within the 0.2 km map-matching tolerance used as a data-layer parameter, so no refund is computed from it; no clause makes it exempt.

23:07:55–23:16:25: trace leaves ECP at ~1.3097,103.9344, runs north-east to ~1.3184,103.9480 and then doubles back south-west through the quoted line's own coordinates in reverse before rejoining at ~1.3124,103.9518; ≈2.0 km of pure deviation. No traffic incident (incidents list empty) and no low speed band (ECP is band 4), so RD-4 does not exempt it; no chat, so RD-3/RD-5 do not apply (driver says his GPS chose it — a claim, not consent, G11). Unmetred extra mileage refundable under RD-1/RD-2.

22:58:25–23:04:25: trace leaves ECP northbound (1.3052,103.8962 → 1.3069,103.9063) and then works back west against the route direction (1.3037,103.9014; 1.3056,103.9102) before rejoining eastbound at ~1.3045,103.9171; ≈2.7 km of extra running. Same analysis as seg2: no RD-4 corroboration, no RD-3 stop and no RD-5 consent, so it counts under RD-1/RD-2.

rejected_claims.reason: "The GPS rerouted me, that's all" is a bare claim; the trace shows long out-and-back running against the route direction with no incident or congestion on record to justify it, and no chat evidence of any route agreement. RD-1/RD-4 place the burden of a reasonable cause on the driver, and neither is met.

The rider asks for the whole 6.49 km / 21.469 → 27.96 km difference ($9.15). RD-2 refunds only the unexempted deviation segments' extra mileage; a portion of the variance is map-matching drift / route-corridor slack (incl. the ~0.3 km tolerance stub) which is not refunded, so the award is $7.41, not $9.15.
